memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot... and together they set out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan. But when they came to Harran, they settled there. Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Harran. - Gen 11:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a sobering ending. Terah set out from Ur "to go to Canaan" - the very land God would promise to Abram. He began the journey. But then comes that heavy little sentence: "when they came to Harran, they settled there." They stopped halfway. Terah never reached Canaan. He lived out his days and died in Harran, short of the destination.

Harran was comfortable. It was a prosperous city on the trade route, a good place to stop. And so a journey toward the promised land ended in a comfortable settlement halfway there. How many of us do the same - starting well, then settling somewhere comfortable, short of everything God intended?

The danger is rarely that we refuse to start. It is that we stop. We set out toward God's purposes, then find a Harran - a comfort, a security, a good-enough place - and we settle. The journey quietly ends, not in dramatic rebellion, but in comfortable stopping.

But the story does not end in Harran. In the very next chapter, God calls Abram to leave Harran and go on. Where Terah settled, Abram would rise and follow - becoming one who lived "in tents" while "looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God" (Heb 11:9-10). Don't settle in Harran. God has more for you than a comfortable stopping place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you settled somewhere comfortable, short of what God intended?
- What "Harran" might God be calling you to leave?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from settling in comfortable places short of Your purposes. Give me courage to keep going where You lead, never trading Your promises for an easy stopping place.
Amen.
